_README: Ongoing story threads for cross-day memory. The cloud agent appends/updates threads each run and prunes stale ones. Format per thread: {"id", "title", "first_seen", "last_update", "summary", "status"}.

threads.title: US-Israel war on Iran
threads.summary: Iran fired missiles at US forces in Jordan (intercepted); US and Saudi jets struck Iran-aligned targets in Iraq in response to prior drone attacks. The confrontation has since broadened into a declared U.S.-Israel war on Iran (launched February 2026): Tehran says the US will 'pay the price' for civilian deaths in a strike on Qeshm island, and NATO jets scrambled July 30 after a Russian missile detonated in Poland amid related regional tension. Aug 1: Trump says fresh US strikes on Iran are coming as soon as this weekend ('we'll be hitting them very hard'); Kuwait says it intercepted Iranian drones that struck a government facility and civilian vehicles, widening the conflict's geographic footprint. A new AP-NORC poll (July 23-27) puts Trump's overall approval at 33%, with about two-thirds of Americans saying the war has not been worth fighting. Aug 2: Trump reversed course, saying he is canceling the planned strikes because 'the perimeters of a deal' have been agreed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end Iran's nuclear program, after Saudi Arabia and other regional powers urged de-escalation; Iranian state media has given no indication Tehran requested the pause or agreed to any new terms, so the reported deal is unconfirmed from Iran's side. Aug 3: Trump says negotiations with Iran formally resume this afternoon; Iranian state media still has not confirmed requesting the pause or agreeing to any terms, so the deal remains unconfirmed from Tehran's side. Separately, Exxon and Chevron reported combined Q2 profits of $26.5B as Brent crude topped $112/barrel amid the conflict, drawing lawmaker criticism as a wartime windfall. Aug 4: Trump held off on renewed strikes, calling it a 'last chance' for Iran to sign a deal; a fourth cargo-ship attack hit a dry bulk vessel off Oman overnight (crew abandoned ship, one seafarer missing). Treasury Secretary Bessent said a Hormuz-reopening deal could land within a day, but Iran's foreign ministry denies any direct US talks are underway, saying it is only discussing a temporary safe shipping route with Oman. Aug 5: Bessent says the US, Iran and Oman are nearing a roughly 60-day interim deal for safe passage through Hormuz, with an announcement possible by Wednesday or Thursday; Trump says talks 'had a very good day' but still warns Iran will be 'hit very hard' absent a deal. Easing oil prices tied to this progress contributed to a record-high Wall Street close the same day. Aug 6: Iran says it's in the 'final stage' of drafting the Oman shipping deal, with a proposed structure of inbound traffic through a northern lane in Iranian waters and outbound through a southern lane in Omani waters, no tolls for the initial 60 days; Trump still says an announcement could come this week, but Tehran blames continued US pressure for the delay and it's unclear whether Washington accepts a deal brokered mainly between Iran and Oman. Aug 7: Iranian-backed proxies targeted Saudi Arabia, widening the conflict's footprint; Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan responded the same day by signing the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, a mutual-defense pact (see separate thread). The advancing Iran-Oman Hormuz deal would bar US and Israeli ships and require compensation from 'hostile' countries. Aug 8: still no finalized joint statement — Iran's foreign ministry says the text remains in final drafting and the deal would not automatically reopen the strait. Aug 9: Iran struck another Gulf tanker (an ADNOC vessel, the 16th such attack), and Iran's foreign minister now explicitly ties a full Hormuz reopening to the US honoring an earlier, disputed June memorandum of understanding rather than just the Oman shipping-lane logistics; the regional footprint widened further as Yemen's military struck Houthi targets and Kuwait intercepted more Iranian drones. Also Aug 9: Pentagon sent a memo to US defense companies as Houthi forces struck Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery. Aug 11: Trump claimed the Strait of Hormuz is now open and demanded Iran pay compensation for war damages; Iran's foreign minister flatly denied any deal, saying there is 'no possibility of restarting negotiations' while the US continues violating the June memorandum and withholds compensation from Iran instead — the two sides' public accounts are now directly contradictory, and oil futures rose on the renewed uncertainty. Aug 12: US forces fired two Hellfire missiles at the steering gear of a Panama-flagged cargo ship after it ignored warnings and tried to sail toward an Iranian port in defiance of the blockade — the first reported direct US military action against a vessel breaching it, rather than an Iranian/Houthi-side tanker attack. Trump now claims '100%'/'total control' of Hormuz and is demanding Iran pay reparations, while Pakistan's defense minister says the two sides are nonetheless nearing 'some sort of an arrangement.' See separate thread for the Gaza/Hamas disarmament deal announced July 31, which runs alongside but is distinct from this war.

threads.title: Mass migrant crossing into Spain's Ceuta
threads.summary: Roughly 60,000 people crossed from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta this week after a Spanish Supreme Court ruling made it harder to turn back migrants arriving by sea; social media posts encouraging the crossing are cited as a contributing factor. Outlets report death tolls ranging from at least 18 to over 60 (drownings and a stampede at a border fence), with most migrants having voluntarily returned to Morocco. Spain's PM is visiting the territory; France has tightened checks on its own border with Spain and Italy has floated suspending Spain from the EU's open-border scheme. Aug 1: Spain confirmed the death toll at 67 and said the situation has been 'almost entirely reversed,' with most migrants having voluntarily returned to Morocco; Spain is installing a 500-meter floating barrier along the border fence, and officials warned of possible additional uncounted casualties on the Moroccan side. Aug 2-3: Confirmed death toll has risen further to 72; roughly 22 EU heads of state have pointed to Spain's mass migrant regularization policy as a 'pull factor' behind the surge. Aug 4: Spain says about 69,500 migrants have now returned to Morocco over four days; Morocco's Interior Ministry blames the surge on social-media misinformation and trafficking networks, and Ceuta is now working through the aftermath (thousands still sheltering, some sleeping on sidewalks) rather than an active influx. Aug 7-9: The dispute escalated into a Spain-Italy Schengen standoff — Italy imposed one month of border checks on Spanish travelers over the Ceuta surge, and Spain retaliated Aug 8 with reciprocal passport/visa checks on Italian travelers (through Sept 7); Italy says it won't lift its checks before Aug 15, and eight European countries now have internal border checks reinstated. Aug 10: New reporting highlights a child-welfare strain in the aftermath — at least 1,342 minors remain among the migrants still present in Ceuta, many unaccompanied, against a stated shelter capacity of only 90 places.

threads.title: Gaza ceasefire / Hamas disarmament deal
threads.summary: Trump announced Hamas agreed, via the Gaza Board of Peace, to a phased disarmament roadmap matched by Israeli withdrawal from Gaza; a detailed plan is due within 14 days. Neither Hamas nor Israel has publicly confirmed. Distinct from, but announced alongside, the ongoing wider US-Israel war on Iran. Aug 3 detail: the roadmap is expected to take 200-250 days, with Gaza police weapons transferred first to a new National Committee, followed by heavier weapons; Israel still hasn't publicly agreed, and Hamas says it won't proceed without a matching Israeli withdrawal. Aug 4: Israeli strikes killed dozens in Gaza over the weekend despite the deal announcement; Israel has conveyed 'serious concerns' about the roadmap to Washington and says it won't withdraw until Hamas is fully disarmed, citing intelligence that Hamas is still rearming and recruiting. Aug 9: Netanyahu moved from voicing concerns to outright rejecting Trump's 15-point Gaza plan, saying Israeli forces won't withdraw until Hamas is 'genuinely disarmed' — the clearest public break yet between Israel and the Trump-brokered roadmap.

threads.title: Hyperscaler AI infrastructure buildout
threads.summary: Google raised 2026 capex guidance to $195-205B; Microsoft/3M, SoftBank France (5GW/E75B), and Chevron/Microsoft Texas power deal all point to accelerating AI data-center investment. Now confirmed: Nvidia is in talks for a ~$250B guarantee backing OpenAI's $500B, 10GW Ohio data-center lease (SoftBank's SB Energy), plus a separate ~$350B facility for OpenAI's chip purchases; analysts have begun calling the structure 'circular financing.' Same week, chip stocks (Nvidia, SK Hynix, Samsung, Micron, AMD, TSMC) shed over $1 trillion in combined market cap on doubts about AI capex sustainability. July 31: investor enthusiasm is concentrating on cloud-infrastructure hosts over model developers, and Microsoft is now positioning itself as a direct competitor to OpenAI/Anthropic (own models, agent tooling) rather than just their host; Q2 GDP data shows AI-related imports (chips, compute hardware) widening the US trade deficit and denting growth (1.5% vs 2.1% prior quarter). Aug 2: First hard demand-side confirmation — Amazon's Q2 earnings show AWS revenue up 37% YoY to $42.2B (vs. 31% expected), its fastest growth in 18 quarters, with AI/chip businesses each topping $25B annualized run rate; Amazon plans $220B in 2026 capex, suggesting the capex buildout still has enterprise demand behind it despite the chip-stock selloff. Aug 3: Global semiconductor industry revenue is projected to top $1 trillion in 2026 for the first time, led by AI-driven demand for computing/data-storage chips (>$500B, +41% YoY) — another demand-side data point alongside the capex/circular-financing debate. Aug 4: Palantir posted 93% YoY Q2 revenue growth ($1.94B) and 149% commercial-revenue growth, crediting demand for 'AI sovereignty' tools; shares jumped ~30% (best day ever) and helped push the S&P 500 toward a record — the first hard evidence this week that customer-facing AI product demand, not just hyperscaler infrastructure capex, is accelerating. Aug 5: The rally continued — S&P 500 closed at a record 7,736.52 (+1.79%) with semiconductor names (Intel, Marvell, Micron, Broadcom) leading gains, suggesting sentiment has swung back from this week's capex-sustainability doubts. Separately, Meta is expanding its Hyperion supercluster in Louisiana to 5GW and entering Canada (Alberta, ~$9B/1GW), and OpenAI announced 'Project Camellia,' a new data-center project in Effingham County, Georgia — continued physical buildout alongside the market-sentiment swings. Qualcomm also cited AI-driven semiconductor/memory supply constraints as the reason it's raising smartphone chip prices double-digits from Sept. 1, a knock-on effect of the buildout reaching consumer hardware pricing. Aug 6: The Nvidia-OpenAI financing web is now reported at roughly $750B combined (the $250B Ohio guarantee plus the chip-purchase facility); new detail shows the Ohio site is a decommissioned uranium-enrichment site on federal land (giving Commerce Dept leverage over its power supply), with an 800MW first phase due 2028 powered by a $33B gas plant Japan has pledged to fund — Nvidia shares fell ~5% on renewed circular-financing criticism, ceding the top market-cap spot back to Apple. Separately, global cloud infrastructure spending hit an 8-year high ($143B in Q2, +$43B, 11th straight quarter of growth), a further demand-side data point for the buildout. Also Aug 6: AMD announced it is acquiring Toronto startup Taalas, which etches trained AI models directly into silicon for large inference-speed gains (claimed ~48x Nvidia H200/B200 throughput on Llama 3.1 8B) at the cost of model-update flexibility — a new front in the buildout beyond raw capex. Anthropic is separately reported hiring an internal AI chip design team. Aug 7: The rally extended to a fresh S&P 500 record close of 7,758, with semiconductor names leading gains on a rebound from the week's earlier chip-stock selloff. Aug 9: First hard quarterly confirmation — SIA reports global semiconductor sales hit $403.3B in Q2 2026 (+35.1% QoQ), and AMD's Q2 revenue jumped 50% YoY to $11.5B (data-center business more than doubled) while AI-connectivity chipmaker Astera Labs grew 104% YoY to $392.4M; Samsung/SK Hynix unveiled new zHBM/high-bandwidth-flash memory architectures targeting AI memory bottlenecks. Separately, Amazon is advancing 'Project Eagle,' a Texas data-center campus, and is investing $48B in India (incl. $21B for cloud/AI infrastructure through 2030); Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta's latest earnings calls shifted emphasis from raw capex totals to time-to-energy and large-scale networking as the practical bottlenecks now limiting buildout speed. Aug 10: Samsung and Broadcom signed a ~$200B, five-year MOU covering HBM4/HBM4E memory, 2nm-and-below foundry manufacturing, and advanced packaging for Broadcom's AI accelerators — a new major foundry relationship alongside TSMC's, against a backdrop of global memory supply constraints. Separately, SpaceX's first earnings report as a public company showed Q2 revenue up 92% YoY to $7.8B (beating estimates) with EBITDA nearly tripling to $3.5B, but shares fell over 7% on investor concern about AI-related capex — echoing the buildout's broader capex-sustainability debate. Aug 10: Meta released Muse Glimmer, an open-weight (Apache 2.0) 30B-parameter agentic model runnable on a single consumer GPU, alongside a Zuckerberg essay framing open-weight AI as a counter to both closed-model rivals and Chinese open-source leadership — a new front in the AI-competition story distinct from Microsoft's direct-competitor positioning noted July 31. Same day, OpenAI expanded its Daybreak cyber-defense program into Blue/Red tiers and released GPT-5.6-Cyber, a purpose-trained cybersecurity model for trusted partners (Accenture, IBM, CrowdStrike, Cloudflare), following Anthropic's earlier cyber-focused model release. Aug 12: Zuckerberg's essay is drawing sustained critical reaction (TechCrunch, CBS and others), with commentary focused on its 'personal superintelligence' framing and Meta's commitment to a 'fully private mode' for users' AI agents; today's coverage is reaction rather than new company news.

threads.title: Japan (Kumamoto) earthquake recovery
threads.summary: Magnitude-7.1 quake near Kumamoto: death toll has climbed from 18 (July 29) to 34 as of July 31. Rescue operations continue at a collapsed shopping mall (Kashima) and a paper mill (Yatsushiro); over 10,000 remain in evacuation shelters, and extreme summer heat combined with water/power outages is raising heatstroke risk for displaced residents. Aug 4: One week on, the death toll holds at 38 (123 injured); response has shifted from search-and-rescue to survivor care, with record heat (40.3C on Aug 3) raising heatstroke risk for the ~9,200 people still in 210 shelters. Tokyo approved about ¥20 billion in reserve funds for relief and infrastructure repair, and the Self-Defense Force has airlifted air coolers to evacuation centers.

threads.title: Fed rate decisions
threads.summary: Fed held its benchmark rate at 3.5%-3.75% for a fifth straight meeting on July 29, with three FOMC members dissenting in favor of a hike. Stocks fell on the news; 30-year Treasury yield hit its highest level since 2007. July 31: Q2 GDP growth came in at 1.5% (down from 2.1%), with AI-driven imports widening the trade deficit; the 30-year mortgage rate hit 6.66% on July 30. Aug 10: July's jobs report showed nonfarm payrolls fell 23,000 (vs. an expected ~83,000 gain) and unemployment ticked up to 4.1%, with May-June revised down a combined 103,000 — new labor-market weakness the Fed will weigh at its next meeting. Aug 12: The July CPI report is due out today, expected to show headline inflation easing slightly to around 3.4% year-over-year — another data point the Fed will weigh alongside the weak jobs report.

threads.title: INC ransomware exploitation of SonicWall SMA VPN flaws
threads.summary: Two SonicWall SMA 1000-series VPN appliance flaws (CVE-2026-15409/15410), chainable for arbitrary command execution, were patched in mid-July 2026. The INC ransomware group has since become the dominant exploiter of the pair, using a custom toolchain (KNUCKLEBALL loader, Suo5 proxy, ORANGETAIL web shell) and listing victims across the US, Australia and the UAE (private sector and government) as recently as August 2. Distinct from the ongoing Cisco SD-WAN and water-utility PLC campaigns. Aug 6: INC's claimed victim count has grown to 885 total; the group has escalated to calling victims directly to pressure payment.

threads.title: JetBrains TeamCity critical unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-63077)
threads.summary: JetBrains disclosed and patched CVE-2026-63077 (CVSS 9.8) on July 27-28: an unauthenticated attacker with HTTP access can exploit TeamCity On-Premises' agent-polling protocol to execute OS commands and read stored credentials, risking CI/CD pipeline integrity. Fixed in 2025.11.7/2026.1.3; JetBrains said it had no evidence of active exploitation at disclosure. Distinct from the Cisco SD-WAN, water-utility PLC, and SonicWall/INC ransomware campaigns tracked separately.

threads.title: Ebola (Bundibugyo strain) outbreak in eastern DRC
threads.summary: WHO puts the outbreak at 3,748 cases and 1,657 deaths as of Aug 1 — the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record and spreading faster than any prior one. Two vaccine efforts have reached human trials: Moderna's mRNA-1469 (Health Canada authorized, first doses given in Canada) and a University of Oxford/Serum Institute of India candidate; Africa CDC is separately planning a trial of Merck's existing Ervebo vaccine (designed for a different Ebola species) as a stopgap. Conclusive trial results are likely still months away. Aug 9: WHO now describes it as the largest Ebola epidemic ever recorded in the DRC, having spread from a single health zone in Ituri province to 49 health zones across five provinces; the US State Department pledged an additional $242 million for response and preparedness on Aug 5. Aug 10: Toll has risen further to roughly 1,850 deaths across 53 of the DRC's 140 health zones; a new treatment center has opened at the heart of the outbreak. Aug 12: Cases and deaths have jumped again, to 4,449 confirmed cases and 2,061 deaths, with 704 patients hospitalized in isolation; officials now call it the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak on record. Neighboring Uganda, by contrast, declared its own related outbreak over on July 28.

threads.title: Russian missile/drone strikes on Kyiv amid interceptor shortage
threads.summary: Aug 1: a Russian barrage of 35 missiles and 185 drones killed 9 in Kyiv, with only 1 of 27 ballistic missiles intercepted. Aug 5: a larger two-hour barrage of 115 drones and 28 missiles killed at least 17; 98 drones were intercepted but no missiles were, underscoring Ukraine's worsening shortage of Patriot interceptors, which Russia has increasingly exploited with near-routine large-scale strikes this summer. Aug 8: a smaller follow-on barrage killed 4 in Kyiv and the surrounding region, continuing the pattern of frequent large-scale strikes. Aug 10: Zelenskyy said Ukraine received only about a third as many Patriot interceptors in H1 2026 as in H1 2025, blaming the shortfall partly on Western supply being diverted to the US-Israel war on Iran. Also Aug 10: a rare reversal in the other direction — a Ukrainian long-range drone strike on an oil facility in Nizhnekamsk, Russia, killed 12-13 people (sources vary), part of Ukraine's own intensifying strikes on Russian energy infrastructure. Aug 12: A large drone attack hit Sevastopol in occupied Crimea, setting a Russian military base on fire; Russian strikes in the Kherson region killed 2 and injured 14 over the prior day, and Ukrainian forces logged 237 combat engagements with Russian troops on Aug 11 — smaller-scale than the Aug 5/8 barrages but part of the same daily pattern.

threads.title: AI embedded in adversary tooling / AI supply-chain attacks
threads.summary: CrowdStrike's 2026 Threat Hunting Report finds AI-enabled adversary activity up 89% YoY: attackers are using AI to generate payloads, exploit AI infrastructure directly, and abuse enterprise LLMs (one campaign sent ~200,000 requests to a model in two minutes). A North Korea-linked group (STARDUST CHOLLIMA) injected malicious code into 131 trusted packages in the open-source Mastra AI agent framework; 87% of H1 2026 software-registry threats involved malicious npm packages. Separately, CISA added a critical Langflow (AI-workflow tool) RCE flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog Aug 5, the latest in a string of Langflow vulnerabilities exploited this year. Aug 9: Check Point reports a Chinese-speaking threat actor has wired a DeepSeek AI agent directly into an autonomous attack pipeline, letting the model itself plan and execute intrusion steps with minimal human direction. Aug 10: A newly disclosed vulnerability class called 'CoreBreak' (presented at Black Hat USA 2026) let attackers forge tool calls directly to AI agents hosted on AWS, Google Cloud, and Vercel, reaching backend tools without the model's authorization — attacking the agent-orchestration layer itself rather than the model; all three vendors have patched. Also Aug 10: researchers described 'vibe hacking,' attackers using coding-assistant AI to speed up exploit development, and OpenAI/Anthropic's dueling cyber-defense model releases (see AI buildout thread) are a direct response to this trend. Distinct from, but thematically related to, the Cisco SD-WAN, water-utility PLC, and SonicWall/INC ransomware threads tracked separately.

threads.title: N-able N-central authentication-bypass exploitation (CVE-2026-18577)
threads.summary: N-able's initial patch for an N-central RMM auth flaw (CVE-2026-18556) proved incomplete; attackers found a bypass, tracked as CVE-2026-18577, letting an unauthenticated attacker gain full admin control of the console and pivot into every managed endpoint. Exploitation was confirmed Aug 2, CISA added it to its KEV catalog Aug 3 with a tight federal patch deadline, and attackers have used access to open persistent Cloudflare tunnels into victim networks. Both on-premises and cloud-hosted deployments are affected; N-able calls impact 'limited,' but researchers report many installs still unpatched.

threads.title: Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (Saudi Arabia-Turkey-Pakistan mutual defense pact)
threads.summary: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a trilateral mutual-defense treaty in Makkah on Aug 7, declaring an attack on one to be an attack on all three — the first such formula among major Muslim-majority militaries since the 1950s Baghdad Pact era. It links NATO's second-largest military (Turkey), the world's top oil exporter (Saudi Arabia), and the only Muslim-majority nuclear power (Pakistan). Signed the same day Iranian-backed proxies reportedly targeted Saudi Arabia, widening the fallout from the ongoing US-Israel war on Iran (tracked separately).

threads.title: Critical, unauthenticated VMware vCenter flaws (CVE-2026-59309/59310)
threads.summary: Broadcom's July 29 VMSA-2026-0006 advisory patches two critical vCenter Server vulnerabilities, both CVSS 9.8: CVE-2026-59309 (auth bypass via VMware Directory Service) and CVE-2026-59310 (directory traversal in the vCenter Syslog Server enabling remote code execution). Also affects ESX, Workstation, Fusion and Cloud Foundation. No workaround exists; only patching to fixed vSphere/Cloud Foundation builds mitigates it. Distinct from the Cisco, SonicWall/INC, TeamCity and N-able incidents tracked separately.

threads.title: Apple Private Cloud Compute path-traversal flaw (CVE-2026-20685)
threads.summary: A now-patched path-traversal flaw (CVE-2026-20685) in Apple's Private Cloud Compute, the backend infrastructure behind Apple Intelligence AI requests, could have let a privileged network attacker write attacker-controlled files as root during node boot. Distinct from the Cisco, SonicWall/INC, TeamCity, N-able and VMware incidents tracked separately.

threads.title: Domestically acquired cyclosporiasis outbreak
threads.summary: CDC says a domestically acquired cyclosporiasis outbreak (tracked since a July 26 report tied it to earlier cuts to federal food-safety monitoring) has expanded to 15 states with 1,645 confirmed cases since May 1, with shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms served at some Taco Bell locations identified as a likely source. A related multistate Salmonella Javiana investigation tied to Sinaloa, Mexico jalapenos distributed by Coast Citrus Distributors is also under FDA/CDC investigation. Aug 3: Michigan reported the outbreak's first two deaths. Aug 5: Michigan said shredded lettuce is back on restaurant menus there as case counts decline in-state, even as the broader multistate outbreak continues elsewhere.

threads.title: Joe Biden's prostate cancer progression
threads.summary: Hunter Biden said in a new interview that Joe Biden's aggressive prostate cancer, diagnosed and announced in May 2025 (after which Biden underwent hormone therapy and radiation), has spread further into his bones and is now 'very painful' and debilitating.

threads.title: Trump-Thune rift over SAVE America Act and August recess
threads.summary: Trump demanded Senate Republicans cancel the five-week August recess to force a vote on his SAVE America Act (a mail-ballot/voter-ID overhaul that has repeatedly failed to find majority support); Majority Leader John Thune refused, backed by most Senate Republicans. Trump has since publicly withheld support for Thune's re-election as GOP leader, escalating the intra-party rift as the chamber heads into recess without acting on the bill. Aug 10: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said Trump's patience is 'running out' with Thune; Thune countered that the Senate has already voted on the bill five times and still lacks the votes, including via reconciliation. Aug 11: no new movement; the Senate remains in recess without a vote. Aug 12: Thune, Trump and Senate conservatives reached a deal to defer the budget-resolution vote until after the August recess while holding an immediate vote on the SAVE Act's voter-ID requirement — easing, for now, the standoff over canceling the recess entirely.

threads.title: Magnitude-7.4 earthquake in western Colombia
threads.summary: A magnitude-7.4 earthquake centered near San Jose del Palmar, about 150 miles west of Bogota, struck western Colombia on Aug 10 — the country's most powerful earthquake this century. The death toll climbed through the day from roughly 47 to 111 to a confirmed 132 (570 injured) as of the latest count, with Pereira alone reporting 60 deaths; Colombia has declared an emergency and officials expect the toll to keep rising as rescue operations continue. Aug 12: The official toll has grown further to 181 dead and 2,595 injured, with 195 people officially listed missing — though civilian-run databases put that figure closer to 4,000, a discrepancy not previously reported. NPR reports the response is straining Colombia's new government and its rescue teams; other outlets (NBC, CNBC) have cited even higher tolls, reflecting how fluid the casualty count remains.

threads.title: Bashar al-Assad sentenced to death in absentia
threads.summary: A Syrian court sentenced former president Bashar al-Assad and his brother, Atef Najib, to death in absentia for crimes against humanity and war crimes committed during Syria's 14-year civil war — one of the first major war-crimes verdicts from Syria's post-Assad judicial process. Assad fled Syria in late 2024 after a rebel offensive ended his family's five-decade rule; the sentence is largely symbolic while he remains outside the country.
